To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the serum sodium concentration is associated with mortality in peritoneal dialysate (PD) patients; 2) this association is independent of the type of PD fluid (glucose- vs. amino-acid-based) and of residual renal function; 3) the serum sodium level at which the association between sodium concentration and mortality is strongest varies by age and gender; and 4) the serum sodium is a stronger predictor of mortality than serum potassium.
